script: My mom forced the teacher to apologize—watch her face when she finally did.. He was in seventh grade, I was in sixth, and our French teacher was the same for every class. She totally hated my older brother. The first time she gave him detention was when he had to bring a cereal box for an assignment. He was on a bad day, said "Stupid box!" and she slapped him with detention. Mom had him hand her a note that read, "I apologize for my son's behavior. We raised him to be respectful to all boxes no matter their size or color. Please forgive him." Fast forward to a night when Dad, hauling an 18‑wheel truck, got into a crash. We rushed to the scene, Dad was fine, but by the time we got back he was exhausted. My brother didn't finish his French homework. The next day, the teacher asks, "Where's your assignment?" He says he couldn't finish it 'cause Dad was in an accident. She snaps, "I don't care. That's not MY problem." (Micro‑hook: "She snapped, 'I don't care.'") He gets detention anyway. After school, he tells Mom the whole thing. She's furious. "You won't serve that detention tomorrow," she says, "I'll take care of it." (Micro‑hook: "I'll take care of it.") The next day, Mom walks straight into the school. No front‑office call, no polite knock. She strides up the stairs, opens the French classroom door, points at the teacher, and shouts, "Get out here. NOW." The teacher steps out, stunned. Mom confronts her. Mom: "He's not serving that detention." Teacher: "Yes, he is. He missed an assignment." Mom: "Because his father was in an accident, we didn't get home until later. He cared about Dad more than a stupid homework assignment. He's not serving detention because he loves his father. Understand?" Teacher: "Fine." Mom: "Good. Now apologize to him." Teacher: "I'll do it after class." Mom: "No. You'll apologize NOW, in front of the whole class. I won't leave until you do." The teacher, defeated, walks back into the room, stands before the class, and apologizes. Mom smiles, satisfied, and leaves. She earned a reputation that day for standing up for us. She'd fight for us again later, but that's another story.
